newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil coop says outlook remains lower coffee crop.
newsitem.headline: Brazil coop says outlook remains lower coffee crop.

text.p: A survey of 400 coffee growers in Brazil's Cooxupe cooperative in Guaxupe, Minas Gerais State, has shown little change in the outlook for a lower coffee crop in 1997/98, said the cooperative's superintendent.
"Our latest survey has repeated the same figures as in our first estimate in November," said Jose Geraldo Rodrigues.
"In our first estimate in November, we forecast a 42 percent drop in relation to 1996/97 and this time it is a 44 percent drop so there really is no change," he added.
The 400 producers were in the south of Minas as well as in part of the state's Cerrado region and part of Sao Paulo state, Rodrigues said.
"The area covered was 24,700 hectares and these producers who harvested 780,749 (60-kg bags) in 1996/97 now anticipate a harvest of 433,586 bags this year," he added.
Rodrigues said the cooperative had no plans to make any estimates for the state of Minas Gerais.
Producer officials maintain that the upcoming national crop will be around 20 million bags while traders' forecast are up to 24 million bags.
